title: Infinite Jest
author: David Foster Wallace
summary: A huge, footnoted novel set in a near-future North America, moving between a Boston halfway house and a junior tennis academy. A rumoured film, so entertaining that viewers cannot look away, haunts the background.
readIf: you want a very long, funny, demanding novel about addiction, entertainment and loneliness and are ready to be patient.
skipIf: you want a plot that resolves neatly, since the book is famously dense, digressive and open-ended.

pairings.reason: Another huge, formally unusual novel with footnotes, obsession and a hidden centre.
A big American family novel about addiction, illness and dysfunction, but far easier to follow.
A comic satire built on loops and absurdity, with a sharp sense of humour.
